四级汇总词汇 · 16英文原文

The Wet Line Under the Market Door

市场大门下的那道水痕 · 650 词 · 8 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1A municipal council planned an extensive renovation of a market near a residential development. An architect named Isha found two doors that had begun to stick. The developer blamed a carpenter who had trimmed them the previous year. Isha asked for a structural inspection before the council approved construction. Both doors leaned in the same direction, and both opened easily after a dry week. If the problem lay under the concrete foundation, another costly door repair would delay the work without making the building safe.

2She studied the blueprint in the lobby. The original framework included four brick pillars and an upper wing. A thin crack ran downward beside a doorway. A bushy plant grew from the gap. The interior ceiling was level, but a pale line of damp ran across the exterior wall. Isha pushed a small inspection wheel along the base of the wall. The reading showed a slight dip near the drainage pipe. The layout made it possible for water from the roof and chimney to reach that corner before it left the site.

3Outside, a heap of garbage had partially covered the outlet. The manager wanted to renovate the entire courtyard. Isha began with containment of hazardous waste. Traders set recyclable cardboard aside and identified a source of pollution near the pipe. Freezing could block the rest of the outlet. The old design was virtually useless if rubbish could reach it from three directions. They cleared each route separately so they could tell which pollutant had accumulated where.

4Water flowed from an adjacent property with a newly paved yard. Higher building density had increased runoff, though there was no skyscraper in sight. A large pipe would require extensive excavation. Isha proposed an economical channel with an accessible grate. It would minimize disruption and make better utilization of a vacant strip. The developer asked whether it could stay open and thereby reduce waste. Isha showed him where workers could clear the grate after a storm instead of depending on a complicated underground pump.

5They tested the scheme with a measured supply of water. At first the level beside the pillar still rose. A contractor found that one bend had been laid too high. He adjusted it rather than dig up the entire system. Once the water had an adequate exit, the team checked the soil for signs of further movement. Isha wanted sufficient evidence before calling the market operational. A quick reduction in damp was beneficial. It did not prove the support beneath the pillar had recovered.

6The project also dealt with water from a path built primarily for visitors. Its proximity to the hall made that runoff important. An expansive paved area could keep shoppers dry while sending more runoff to the market. Isha proposed planting part of it to hold water. The developer wanted a more monumental entrance. A planner asked what improvement was vital at that stage. They agreed to oversee the drain test before deciding how much ground to build on.

7Another heavy rain became a critical test. The channel held water briefly, then released it. Workers did intensive repairs to the pillar. A temporary entrance gave them room to reopen one wing. Management agreed to inspect the grate weekly and keep an ample path clear. Getting rid of that source of garbage would enhance the effect of the renovation. The market could operate without the creation of a greenhouse.

8A carpenter finally adjusted the doors. A trader mopped the lobby and asked about a dent beneath the sill. The architect showed her how rain from the neighboring estate had flowed downhill. The hall had been built partly over a former channel. A worker had mopped around the mark, and the floor presently showed a clue that the plans missed. Foresight meant keeping that clue visible. The council assigned a worker responsible for watching it, so the same setback would be noticed early.

四级汇总词汇 · 16中文译文

市场大门下的那道水痕

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1市议会打算大修住宅区旁的一座市场。建筑师伊莎发现两扇门开始卡住。开发商怪去年来修门的木匠。议会批准施工前，伊莎要求先查结构。两扇门朝同一方向歪，连晴一周又都好开了。要是问题在混凝土地基下面，再花钱修门只会耽误进度，建筑也不会因此变安全。

2她在门厅研究蓝图。原结构有四根砖柱和楼上一侧的房间。门边一条细裂缝向下延伸，缝里长出一簇枝叶。室内天花板很平，外墙却横着一道浅水印。伊莎沿墙根推过一只小测量轮，读数显示排水管旁地面微微下陷。现有布局让屋顶和烟囱流下的水先汇到这个墙角，再离开场地。

3外面一堆垃圾遮住了部分出口。经理想把整个院子重做。伊莎先控制有害废弃物。商贩把能回收的纸板分出来，确认管边的污染来源。结冰会堵住剩下的空隙。垃圾若能从三个方向涌来，原设计几乎起不到作用。他们分别清通每条路线，弄清哪些污染物积在哪儿。

4新铺过的邻院也有水流过来。周围虽没有摩天楼，房子盖得更密了，地面径流随之增加。换大管得大挖一场。伊莎提出更省钱的水沟方案，加一道够得着的格栅。这样能减少对市场的影响，还能利用闲置地带。开发商问，能否靠它减少闭市和浪费。伊莎指给他看，暴雨后工人可以直接清格栅，无须依靠复杂的地下泵。

5他们用量过的水测试。起初砖柱边的水位还是升了。一处弯管铺得太高，承包工调低了它，避免重挖整个系统。排水顺了，大家再查土壤有没有移动。伊莎要有充分证据才能说市场可以营业。潮气快速减少是好事，却不能证明柱子下的支撑已经恢复。

6工程还得处理游人步道的水。步道离大厅太近，径流也很重要。铺出宽阔地面能让顾客走得干爽，却可能把更多水送向市场。伊莎建议留一部分种植物蓄水。开发商想要更气派的入口。规划人员问，现阶段最要紧的是哪一项改动。大家同意先监督排水试验，再决定盖多少。

7又一次大雨成了关键考验。水沟短暂存水，随后顺利排走。工人集中修砖柱，临时入口让一侧市场先开起来。管理方同意每周检查格栅，保留足够宽的通道。把垃圾来源控制住，翻修才会长久见效。市场可以重新经营，不必另外建温室。

8最后，木匠调正了两扇门。商户拖地时问起门槛下的凹痕。伊莎带她看，邻近住宅区的雨水怎样往下流。大厅有一部分建在旧水道上。有人绕开痕迹拖地，因此图纸遗漏的线索还留在地面。提前想一步，就是让这个标记继续看得见。议会安排一人留意，免得同样的问题又拖到最后才发现。
